newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan April export orders up 5.91 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan April export orders up 5.91 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Foreign orders for Taiwan goods rose 5.91 percent to US$10.490 billion in April compared to April 1996, the economics ministry said on Wednesday.
The rise in April export orders, while modest in percentage terms, was sharply higher than an average forecast for a 2.548 percent rise that resulted from a May 20 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.

At US$10.49 billion, the total value of export orders in April was the second highest on record, reflecting increasing demand for Taiwan-made telecommunications products, the ministry said in its monthly summary report.
April orders were only slightly below Taiwan's monthly record of US$10.51 billion set in September 1996.
The following is a table of export order data in million of U.S. dollars:

Geographically, the United States remained Taiwan's biggest market with export orders rising 11.38 percent to $3.13 billion. Information and telecommunication products topped the island's main exports to the United States.
Hong Kong was next with orders totalling $2.03 billion, up 7.13 percent from April 1996.

Orders from Japan, Taiwan's main pork export destination, were down 14.38 percent to $1.19 billion due to a official ban on Taiwan pork imports following the island's March 20 outbreak of a hog foot and mouth disease.
European orders rose 9.71 percent to $1.59 billion.
In sectoral term, telecommunication and information products orders jumped 30.27 percent to $1.72 billion, followed by electronics products, up 8.49 percent to $1.47 billion.
Textile orders grew 2.65 percent to $1.36 billion, while base metal products increased 5.25 percent to $920 million.
Plastics and rubber orders decreased by 2.74 percent to $670 million, while machinery orders were down 5.69 percent to 40 million.
